_comment: Site registry. Structure, not secrets - this belongs in git precisely
because it must be reviewable, diffable and testable.
The octet is the site's identity on the overlay network: it owns
10.<octet>.0.0/16. Two sites sharing one collides on the tailnet and
presents as a broken network rather than a configuration mistake, so
uniqueness is asserted at plan time - see registry.tf. An octet must never
be recycled either: routes for a retired site can linger and would start
Valid range is 1-95. Kubernetes defaults put services at 10.96.0.0/12 and
pods at 10.244.0.0/16; those are cluster-internal and never routed over the
overlay, but overlapping them makes debugging needlessly confusing.
Site keys are codes, not client names. What each code belongs to, and the
hypervisors behind it, live in the fleet document in the vault.
